**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Continues to accept 'original, unpublished texts in French or English, in any field, discipline or method of philosophy' with no thematic restriction; publishes both spontaneously submitted individual articles and occasional thematic/tribute issues chosen freely by researchers (per journal's own submission-guidelines page). Recent tracked article titles (via Philosophy Paperboy aggregator, undated but recent feed) span history of philosophy and contemporary topics: e.g. "(Auto)portraits entre deux robes," "Mapping the Boundaries of Conscious Life in Margaret Cavendish's Philosophy," "La doctrine du concept chez Husserl," "The Neoplatonism of Evagrius Ponticus" — consistent with a broad, non-specialized general philosophy journal rather than one with a narrow current focus.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** history of philosophy (ancient, medieval, modern figures e.g. Husserl, Evagrius Ponticus, Cavendish), any philosophical method/discipline, no restriction stated (per official scope: 'toute méthode philosophique'), thematic/tribute issues honoring individual scholars (e.g. 125th-anniversary volume honoring Anne Fagot-Largeault and Dominique Perler; issue honoring Michel Dupuis on care ethics and philosophical anthropology)
